historical_references.reference: Victariel is believed to be a variant of the name Victor, which was a popular name in the Early Christian period. Victor means 'victor' in Latin and was given to boys who were believed to have the strength and courage of a victor. This name was particularly favored during the Roman Empire and the early Middle Ages when Christianity was gaining popularity.

historical_references.reference: Another theory suggests that the name Victariel may have originated from the Celtic name Guicthelin or Gwitheline, which means 'strong, victorious one'. Some historians believe that the Christian name Victariel may have been a fusion of the Celtic and Latin names, reflecting the cultural influences of the time.
